summary: A resident brings up how the paper printed the result of a local race, naming the winner or only saying how it came out.
realLife: Local papers printed the count the morning after: a Detroit mayor won with nearly 80 percent of the vote while only about 20 percent of voters turned out; a Rochester, Minnesota mayor won by 1.2 percent; Lewiston, Maine's mayoral runoff was decided by 122 votes in the lowest runoff turnout since at least 1980.
sources: WXYZ Detroit, Detroiters react to the city's next mayor: https://www.wxyz.com/news/uplift-the-city-detroiters-react-to-mary-sheffields-historic-win-to-become-citys-next-mayor
KTTC, Rochester mayoral candidates share reactions to election results: https://www.kttc.com/2026/11/04/rochester-mayoral-candidates-share-reactions-election-results/?outputType=amp
inGame: election-result named, unnamed and known in the bring-it-up rows: the speaker says which paper printed the race for {seat} and, if they remember, who took it.

turns.pull: the result is on the speaker's record
turns.writes: writes who took the race, as a fact

turns.turn: The speaker only saw the story
turns.pull: the speaker read the paper but the name is not on their record
turns.writes: writes how it came out, without the name
